THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, PRAYING TO QUASH THE PROCEEDINGS PENDING ON THE FILE OF THE LEARNED I ADDL.

CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, KUNDAPURA IN CRIME NO.275/2015 DATED 04.12.2015 AND SUBSEQUENT CHARGE SHEET IN C.C.NO.51/2016 DATED 21.03.2016 FILED UNDER SECTIONS 498A, 34 OF IPC R/W SECTIONS 3,4 OF THE DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT, 1961.

THIS CRIMINAL PETITION COMING ON FOR HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 3  ORDER

The petitioners have been charge sheeted for the offences under Sections 498A and 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, alleging that the defacto complainant is the legally wedded wife of the accused No.1.
The accused Nos.2 and 4 are the sisters-in-laws and accused No.3 is the mother-in-law of the defacto complainant.
The accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty, both mentally and physically, and also demanded to bring money from the parental home.
The cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate for the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.

Sri Umesh vs Smt Shobha on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137627173/
2 2.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 4 has filed an application under Section 320 of Cr.PC read with Section 482 of Cr.PC stating that the accused No.1 and the defacto complainant have amicably settled the dispute in MC No.124/2022 and in terms of the settlement, the marriage of the defacto complainant and the accused No.1 has been dissolved subject to payment of Rs.10,25,000/- towards permanent alimony.
In the said settlement, the defacto complainant has stated that she has agreed to withdraw the criminal proceeding initiated against the accused herein.

3. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non- compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that the accused No.1 and the defacto complainant have amicably settled the dispute between among themselves, it will be a futile exercise to continue the criminal proceedings since the probability of conviction of the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 4 is remote and bleak in view of the settlement arrived between the parties.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in CC No.1999/2016 pending on the file of the I Addl.
Civil Judge and JMFC, Kundapura, insofar as the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 4 is hereby quashed.
iii) Liberty is reserved with the 2nd respondent to revive this petition, in the event,
the petitioners fails to comply with the terms and conditions contained in the petition under Section 13(B)(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, for dissolving the marriage by mutual consent.
Sd/-
